explanation: Seasons come from Earth's tilt of about 23.4 degrees, which angles each hemisphere towards the Sun in turn. Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January, in the northern winter.

claims.text: Earth's seasons are caused by the tilt of its axis, not by changes in its distance from the Sun.
Earth's axis is tilted by about 23.4 degrees.
Earth is closest to the Sun in early January.
Because of the tilt, each hemisphere leans towards the Sun for part of the year and away from it for the rest.
